title: The Ring of Fire is not one bad day: 2024's densest cell shook on 360 days out of 366.
source: Source: USGS Earthquake Catalog (earthquake.usgs.gov), magnitude 4.0+, worldwide, 2024
legendCaption: Earthquakes per cell, cumulative through the year (count, not energy or magnitude) —
conclusion: 1,720 events in one cell, on 360 of 366 days — its busiest day carried 18.
caveat: A hexagon appears on the day its first magnitude-4 event was catalogued, and darkens as its running count crosses each class — an absent cell means "nothing catalogued yet", never "no earthquakes here". Count is not energy: a cell of hundreds of M4 events outranks one holding a single M7.5. 102 of the 14,175 catalogued events fall outside this frame, poleward of 61°S–78°N.
alt: A world map of 2024's magnitude-4-or-greater earthquakes, binned into 149 equal hexagons and played through the year one day at a time. Cells trace the Pacific plate boundaries: 91 of the 149 cells have already appeared within the first 30 days, and the picture thickens rather than changing shape. The densest cell, outlined in the accent colour off the Fiji–Tonga trench, ends the year holding 1,720 events against a median non-empty cell of 13 — and those 1,720 fall on 360 of the year's 366 days, with the busiest single day carrying 18 of them, so the cell is continuously active rather than the record of one aftershock sequence. Its events are catalogued by USGS as Fiji 49% and Tonga 36%.
